  "title": "AQA A-level Psychology Paper 1: Introductory topics in psychology (7182/1) — Practice Paper",
  "instructions": [
    "Answer all questions in Section A, Section B, Section C and Section D.",
    "The paper carries 96 marks in total.",

  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "q1",
      "label": "Question 1",
      "prompt": "Which of the following is a definition of conformity? Shade one circle only.\n\nA A change in a person's behaviour or opinions as a result of real or imagined pressure from a person or group of people.\nB A change in a person's behaviour or opinions as a result of pressure from an authority figure.\nC A change in a person's behaviour or opinions as a result of reinforcement from a group of people.\nD A change in a person's behaviour or opinions as a result of internal conflict.",
      "marks": 1,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q2",
      "label": "Question 2",
      "prompt": "Identify the type of conformity shown in each of the following examples. Write one letter (C, I or N) in each blank.\n\nC = compliance  I = identification  N = internalisation\n\n2.1 A student joins a demonstration because they genuinely believe in the cause and continues to support it after the demonstration ends. ____\n2.2 A teenager laughs at a joke they do not find funny because their friendship group is laughing. ____\n2.3 A new employee adopts the working practices of their team because they want to be accepted by the group, but changes them when they move to a different team. ____",
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q3",
      "label": "Question 3",
      "prompt": "Outline the authoritarian personality as an explanation of obedience. [4 marks]",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q4",
      "label": "Question 4",
      "prompt": "Discuss research into situational variables affecting obedience. [8 marks]",
      "marks": 8,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q5",
      "label": "Question 5",
      "prompt": "A psychologist investigated whether the presence of other people affects helping behaviour. Participants were observed in a simulated emergency. In Condition A, each participant believed they were the only person who could hear the emergency. In Condition B, each participant believed four other people could also hear the emergency. The psychologist recorded whether or not each participant went for help.\n\nThe psychologist used a significance level of 0.05 and the calculated value of the test statistic fell beyond the critical value. The psychologist concluded that the presence of other people significantly reduces helping behaviour.\n\n5.1 Identify the dependent variable in this study. [1 mark]\n5.2 Explain one reason why the psychologist used an observed (laboratory) setting in this study. [2 marks]\n5.3 Other than the setting, outline one way in which the study could be improved. [2 marks]\n5.4 Explain one limitation of collecting quantitative data in this study. [2 marks]",
      "marks": 7,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q6",
      "label": "Question 6",
      "prompt": "Discuss the role of social influence processes in social change. [8 marks]",
      "marks": 8,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q7",
      "label": "Question 7",
      "prompt": "Outline the multi-store model of memory. [4 marks]",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q8",
      "label": "Question 8",
      "prompt": "A psychologist carried out a study of the effects of anxiety on the accuracy of eyewitness testimony. Participants watched a video of a violent crime. One group was given a questionnaire containing a question about the weapon used. The other group was given a questionnaire without this question. The psychologist measured the accuracy of each participant's recall of details of the crime.\n\nThe psychologist found that participants who answered the question about the weapon were less accurate in their recall of other details of the crime than participants who did not answer this question.\n\n8.1 Identify the independent variable in this study. [1 mark]\n8.2 Explain one ethical issue that the psychologist should have considered in this study. [2 marks]\n8.3 Explain how the findings of this study might be explained with reference to the weapon focus effect. [3 marks]\n8.4 Discuss one limitation of this study in terms of its generalisability to real-life eyewitnesses. [3 marks]",
      "marks": 9,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q9",
      "label": "Question 9",
      "prompt": "Discuss research into the effects of misleading information on the accuracy of eyewitness testimony. [8 marks]",
      "marks": 8,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q10",
      "label": "Question 10",
      "prompt": "Outline what is meant by the terms 'proactive interference' and 'retroactive interference' in memory. [4 marks]",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q11",
      "label": "Question 11",
      "prompt": "A psychologist investigated the effects of two types of interference on recall. Group 1 learned a list of 20 words, then learned a second list of 20 words from the same category (animals). Group 2 learned a list of 20 words, then learned a second list of 20 words from a different category (vehicles). All participants were then asked to recall the first list of words.\n\nThe mean number of words correctly recalled by Group 1 was 7. The mean number of words correctly recalled by Group 2 was 12.\n\n11.1 Calculate the difference between the two means. Show your working. [1 mark]\n11.2 Explain one reason why the psychologist used two different categories of words in this study. [2 marks]\n11.3 Explain how the results of this study support interference as an explanation of forgetting. [3 marks]",
      "marks": 6,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q12",
      "label": "Question 12",
      "prompt": "Outline what is meant by 'eyewitness testimony' and explain one factor that affects the accuracy of eyewitness testimony. [4 marks]",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q13",
      "label": "Question 13",
      "prompt": "A psychologist carried out a study of the effects of two types of interview technique on the accuracy of recall. Participants watched a video of a crime and were then interviewed using either a standard interview or a cognitive interview. The psychologist recorded the number of correct details recalled by each participant.\n\nThe psychologist used a significance level of 0.05 and the calculated value of the test statistic fell beyond the critical value. The psychologist concluded that the cognitive interview produces significantly more accurate recall than the standard interview.\n\n13.1 Outline what is meant by the term 'cognitive interview'. [4 marks]\n13.2 Other than the type of interview, identify one extraneous variable that the psychologist should have controlled in this study and explain how it could be controlled. [2 marks]\n13.3 Explain one strength of the cognitive interview in terms of its practical application in real-life police interviews. [2 marks]",
      "marks": 8,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q14",
      "label": "Question 14",
      "prompt": "Outline what is meant by the term 'reciprocity' in the context of caregiver–infant interactions. [3 marks]",
      "marks": 3,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q15",
      "label": "Question 15",
      "prompt": "A psychologist observed caregiver–infant interactions in a laboratory setting. The psychologist recorded the number of interactions that showed reciprocity and the number that showed interactional synchrony. The psychologist used two observers and calculated the correlation between their records to check inter-observer reliability.\n\n15.1 Explain one reason why the psychologist used two observers in this study. [2 marks]\n15.2 Explain one strength of observing caregiver–infant interactions in a controlled observation. [2 marks]\n15.3 Explain one limitation of using controlled observations to study caregiver–infant interactions. [2 marks]",
      "marks": 6,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q16",
      "label": "Question 16",
      "prompt": "Outline the role of the internal working model in later relationships. [4 marks]",
      "marks": 4,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q17",
      "label": "Question 17",
      "prompt": "Discuss research into the influence of early attachment on later relationships. [8 marks]",
      "marks": 8,
      "assets": []
    },
    {
      "id": "q18",
      "label": "Question 18",
      "prompt": "Outline what is meant by the term 'maternal deprivation'. [2 marks]",
      "marks": 2,
      "assets": []
    },
    "q19",
      "label",
      "prompt",
      "marks",
      "assets"
    ],
      "id": "q19",
      "label": "Question 19",
      "prompt": "A psychologist studied a group of children who had spent time in an institution in early childhood. The psychologist compared the attachment type of these children with the attachment type of a group of children raised in their own families. The psychologist used the Strange Situation procedure to classify each child as securely attached, insecure-avoidant or insecure-resistant.\n\nThe psychologist found that a higher proportion of the institutionalised children were classified as insecure-avoidant than the family-raised children.\n\n19.1 Outline what is meant by 'institutionalisation' in the context of attachment. [2 marks]\n19.2 Explain one reason why the Strange Situation procedure might not be an appropriate way to assess attachment in institutionalised children. [2 marks]\n19.3 Explain one way in which the findings of this study might be explained with reference to the critical period for attachment. [3 marks]",
      "marks": 7,
      "assets": []
    }
